newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian gold closes easier following world trend.
newsitem.headline: Indian gold closes easier following world trend.

text.p: ** Gold 24 carat closed 15 rupees lower at 4,755 rupees per 10 gramme against Saturday's close, reflecting world price decline, fresh offerings and dull seasonal demand.
** Prices of a gold biscuit (116.50 gramme) closed 150 rupees lower at 55,650 rupees per piece after losing 100 rupees on Saturday.
** Silver (.999) closed 10 rupees lower at 6,830 rupees per kg amid fresh arrivals while industrial demand was at a low ebb. Silver was down by 90 rupees per kg on Saturday.

Gold 24 carat closed 15 rupees lower at 4,755 rupees per 10 gramme on Monday against Saturday's close. Sliding global prices prompted fresh unloading by the local stockists facing dull seasonal demand, dealer said.
Gold fell 10 rupees on Saturday. Fresh arrivals of imported gold remained low today and trading volume remained poor during the day.
Prices of a gold biscuit (116.50 gramme) closed 150 rupees lower at 55,650 rupees per piece against the previous close of 55,800 rupees after losing 100 rupees per piece on Saturday.

Silver (.999) closed 10 rupees lower at 6,830 rupees per kg against the previous close of 6,840 rupees as fresh arrivals dragged prices lower while industrial demand remained dull during the day. Silver was down by 90 rupees per kg on Saturday.

"Sentiment at the close remained subdued but looking at the reports that silver prices in the world market have bounced back, the local market may recover recent losses in the coming days," one broker said. (Conversion $1=35.77 rupees)
